Upstream `Blocked-by: objectstack#9340` is MERGED, so the card is dispatchable in principle; the **dispatch gate is the pin**, exactly as the card's own "Dispatch condition" states — before claiming, probe that the consumed `@objectstack/spec` build exports `ListMapConfigSchema`, and note the current pin lag (objectstack#8893 tracks the lockfile still resolving a pre-GA spec). If the pin doesn't cover objectstack#9370 yet, park the claim rather than building against a vendored spec that lacks the key.

Serial-constraint note for the claim: `ObjectMap.tsx` is a declared hot file (in-flight map family: #5017 queued, #5018 in the decision inbox) — this card's surface is `ListView.tsx` forwarding + switcher wiring, which should not touch `ObjectMap.tsx` internals; if measurement says otherwise, respect the hot-file serial queue on the seat post. The "Done when" list includes the objectstack-side liveness-ledger flip (`planned` → `live`) as a follow-up card filed on the objectstack queue by the accepting seat, per cross-repo rule 3. Size/model suggestion: S–M / opus.

**PM dispatch-gate probe (2026-08-18 ~21:02Z, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`): still blocked — but the reason has changed, so the earlier comment's rationale no longer applies.**

The 08:06Z probe concluded "the pin is `17.0.0-rc.2`, which predates objectstack#9370". **The pin has since moved** — and the gate still fails anyway.

## Measured

```
$ git show origin/main:pnpm-lock.yaml | grep -oE "@objectstack/spec@[0-9][^'\":()]*" | sort -u
@objectstack/spec@17.0.0            # was 17.0.0-rc.2 at 08:06Z
```

So the specifier is now `^17.0.0` and the lockfile resolves **GA 17.0.0**, not an rc. The earlier comment's reasoning — "rc.2 predates the landing" — is spent.

Probed the published tag directly, in `objectstack`:

```
$ git grep -n "ListMapConfigSchema" @objectstack/spec@17.0.0 -- packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts
(no output)

$ git grep -c "ListViewSchema"      @objectstack/spec@17.0.0 -- packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts
17                                   # counter-probe: file and tag are real

$ git grep -c "ListMapConfigSchema"  origin/main -- packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts
4                                    # present on main
```

**`ListMapConfigSchema` is on objectstack `main` but NOT in the published `17.0.0` build.** objectstack#9370 landed after the GA cut, so a consumer pinned to `^17.0.0` still cannot see the key.

⛔ **Still not dispatchable.** Unblocking now requires a spec release *after* #9370 plus a pin bump here — not merely the pin moving off `rc.2`, which has already happened and was not enough.

## Two notes for whoever re-probes next

**Do not probe `node_modules`.** I tried first; `@objectstack/spec` is not installed in this container, so both the probe **and** the counter-probe came back empty. An empty probe with an empty counter-probe is not a reading — it looked exactly like "the symbol is absent" while proving nothing.

**The file is `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`, not `view.ts`.** My first tag probe used the wrong path and returned zero with a zero counter-probe; the reading was void and I had to redo it. The counter-probe is what caught both mistakes.

The card's own instruction stands and is worth repeating: **re-run the probe each round; do not dispatch on the strength of `Blocked-by:` being MERGED.** Merged upstream ≠ published ≠ pinned here. Three distinct states, and this card has now been stopped by two of them.

Pin lag is tracked at objectstack#8893.

Nothing about this card's own diagnosis has changed — the 2026-08-18 21:02Z probe above still stands. What has changed is that the blocker now has a **name and a mechanical unlock**, so this card no longer needs to be re-probed by hand every round.

## It is the same blocker as #5074, and it is not specific to this key

Measured this round:

| reading | value |
| --- | --- |
| objectui `pnpm-lock.yaml` → `@objectstack/spec` | **`17.0.0`**, lockfile-exact under `^17.0.0` |
| objectstack `packages/spec/package.json` on `main` | still **`17.0.0`** |
| unreleased changesets in objectstack `.changeset/` | **303** |

So the general shape is: **a spec key merged to objectstack `main` after the 17.0.0 GA cut is invisible to this repo, and will stay invisible until a release happens and the lockfile refreshes.** `ListMapConfigSchema` (objectstack#9370) is one such key; `GanttConfigSchema.viewMode` (objectstack#9463, blocking #5074) is another, found independently this round. Two cards, one cause.

**#5328** records that cause with a machine-readable `Restart-when:` line, so this card comes back automatically instead of costing a probe per round. ⛔ #5328 does not authorise anyone to cut a release — that is a maintainer action.

## What survives from the probe history, because it is worth not re-learning

The three-state distinction this card has now been stopped by twice: **merged upstream ≠ published ≠ pinned here.** The 08:06Z probe concluded "the pin is `rc.2`, which predates the landing"; the pin has since moved to GA `17.0.0` and the gate **still** fails, so that rationale was spent and had to be re-derived. And the counter-probe discipline earned its keep twice on this card — once when `node_modules` was absent (probe *and* counter-probe both empty, which looks exactly like "the symbol is absent" while proving nothing), once when the path was `view.ts` instead of `view.zod.ts`.

Whoever picks this up when #5328 closes: **re-run the consumption probe against the newly pinned build** before writing code. ⛔ Do not dispatch on the strength of `Blocked-by:` being closed alone — that is the mistake this card exists to document.

Pin lag is also tracked at objectstack#8893.

## Unblocked — premise re-verified on the merged ref and it **still holds**

Unlock scan by the **spec@objectui** seat after PR #5529 merged. Checked against `origin/main` @ `2d36552d2`, not taken from the card text.

### Blocker discharged

`ListMapConfigSchema` (objectstack#9340) shipped in `@objectstack/spec@17.1.0`, and this repo now **pins** it: lockfile resolves 17.1.0 for all six `@objectstack/*` packages, with 0 entries left at 17.0.0. All three states — merged upstream / published / pinned here — are finally true. `Blocked-by: objectui#5328` discharged; `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`.

### The card's substance survives the pin

Measured on merged main: **`ListMapConfigSchema` has zero references anywhere in `packages/` or `apps/`.** The spec-declared, view-level `map` block is still authorable and still inert at runtime — exactly what this card says.

### ⚠️ One thing that will look like the fix and is not

`ListView.tsx:2143` **does** forward map config today:

```
locationField: schema.options?.map?.locationField || 'location',
...pickFlatMapConfig(schema.options?.map),
```

That is a **different path**: `schema.options.map`, described in its own comment as "an untyped bag", fed through the whitelisted flatten added by objectui#5177. It is not the spec's typed view-level block, and it is not a partial implementation of this card.

Whoever picks this up: do not read that call site as "already done", and do not fold the typed block into the options bag — the point of `ListMapConfigSchema` is that the view-level shape is declared and validated, which the bag by construction is not. The relationship between the two paths (does the typed block replace the bag, or compose with it?) is the first thing to settle, and the answer may be worth a decision card rather than a guess.

Switcher wiring, as the title says, is in scope.

## PM ruling — **A**, per-key merge, and my dispatch named a file it had not verified

### The precedence question: **A**

The dispatch said "follow the sibling visualization blocks' convention" and you measured that the siblings **agree on direction and disagree on granularity** — five merge per key, two (`tree`, `chart`) replace wholesale. So "follow the siblings" underdetermined the answer, exactly as you say. Ruling A, and the deciding argument is the structural one, not a majority vote:

**The two `||` siblings consume a single config object wholesale; the five that merge flatten individual keys into props — and `map` is in the second class.** `getMapConfig` reads seven independent keys. So the granularity of the merge should match the granularity of the read, and it does.

B is not merely different, it has a **measured failure mode**: on the ADR-0047 interface-page path the coordinate binding is **auto-derived, not authored**, so a partial authored block (`map: { titleField }`) would silently replace the derivation, drop `locationField`, and render a map with no markers at all. "The typed block replaces the untyped bag" is a cleaner sentence and a worse contract.

Noted for the record: the 2026-08-22 unblock comment said this relationship might deserve a decision card rather than a guess, and my ruling told you to match the siblings instead. **That ruling was underdetermined and you were right to flag rather than silently pick.** A is cheap to reverse if the maintainer prefers B — one expression plus two test arms.

### My dispatch named the wrong file, and you measured it

Ruling 3 sent you at "the showcase map view's `allowedVisualizations`". That metadata lives in the **framework repo** (`examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/task-visualizations.pages.ts`), where `TaskMapPage` already declares `allowedVisualizations: ['map']` correctly — so there was no objectui change of that shape to make. This is the same class of error as the fences I got wrong earlier today: **naming a location without resolving it first.**

What you found instead is the switcher gap that actually exists in this repo, and it is sharper than the one I described: **the capability gate read `options.map` alone**, so a view binding its coordinates in the spec block was filtered out of *its own* `allowedVisualizations` and fell back to `['grid']` — the feature disabled by the very config that enables it. Making the gate ask **the same merged config the render seam forwards** is the right fix, because it makes the two structurally incapable of disagreeing rather than merely agreeing today.

Ruling 5 held up: the liveness ledger does live in the spec repo, and filing objectstack#11442 with its own flip condition beats editing another repo's ledger from here.

### On the verification

- **The discriminating pin is end-to-end, not a spy**: the real `ListView` driving the real `ObjectMap`, asserting *consequences* — marker title and description read from the declared fields, and a declared camera **suppressing the fit** (bounds undefined, exact lat/lng/zoom). A spy on "was the prop passed" would have proven the plumbing and nothing about the feature.
- **You relabelled one of your own controls after it went red.** An arm named `CONTROL: a declared camera…` turned out to author a view-level block, so it discriminates and is now labelled so. A mislabelled control is worse than a missing one — it launders a discriminating leg as evidence of stability — and catching it in your own suite is the habit that keeps a report worth reading.
- **`check-spec-symbol-derivation`'s green was not leaned on**, per the #5899 caveat; the no-mirror claim comes from the direct `LIST_VIEW_LOCAL_OVERRIDES` measurement instead. That is the correct use of a gate whose coverage is known to be partial.
- **The no-rebuild claim is proved by the red itself**: a dist-resolved suite would have stayed green under a source-only mutation. That is a stronger argument than reciting the alias table.
- **Lint was not narrowed** — the full scan ran, and the 89 pre-existing errors were shown to be in packages carrying no `lint` script, which `turbo run lint` skips by design, with all five changed files counter-probed as present in the run.

### The three filings

All three are correctly routed and unqueued: objectstack#11442 (liveness flip, spec repo), objectstack#11443 (the showcase page's own missing `map` block — the framework half of this card's "Done when", and why this PR alone does not change that page), and objectui#5909 (`defaultMapFromObject` derives no marker-title binding, unlike its three siblings — correctly called a design call about *which field is the title* rather than a one-liner). ⛔ None queued by this seat.

PR #5908 lands at its gate window.
